stories.title: Foreign dignitaries gather in Islamabad for the 30th ECO ministerial meeting
stories.summary:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and multiple international delegates arrived in Islamabad to participate in the 30th Economic Cooperation Organisation Council of Ministers meeting. Upon landing, the Iranian foreign minister was welcomed at the airport by Additional Foreign Secretary Muhammad Tariq Wazir and other foreign ministry officials. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar hosted a welcome dinner on Sunday for the visiting foreign ministers and delegation heads, emphasizing close bonds among member states and Pakistan's dedication to regional cooperation, peace, and progress.

Diplomatic activity in the capital began on Saturday with the arrival of Tahsin Ertugruloglu, Foreign Minister of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus. Additional high-level arrivals included Turkey's Deputy Foreign Minister and delegation head Musa Kulaklikaya, Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Deputy Secretary General Ahmad Saidmurodzoda, Organisation of Islamic Cooperation Secretary General Ismail Ould Cheikh Ahmed, Azerbaijan’s Deputy Foreign Minister Elnur Mammadov, and Kazakhstan’s Deputy Foreign Minister Arman Issagaliyev.

On the sidelines of the summit, Deputy Prime Minister Dar met with ECO Secretary General Dr Asad Majeed Khan. During their discussion, Dar stressed the significance of regional connectivity and economic integration, outlining Pakistan's chairmanship theme, "Reviving Regionalism for a Resilient ECO," and confirming plans to host the ECO Summit in 2027. Dr Khan praised Pakistan's hospitality, arrangements, and coordination for the event.

In a separate meeting, Dar welcomed the OIC secretary general on his maiden visit to Islamabad since taking office. The discussions focused on reinforcing the OIC as a unified voice for the Muslim Ummah. The OIC chief commended Pakistan's diplomatic mediation during the Iran-United States conflict, as well as its active contributions to scientific and technological cooperation through Comstech.

stories.title: Russian air defenses intercept over 100 drones targeting Moscow overnight
stories.summary:
Russian air defense systems intercepted more than 100 drones aimed at Moscow overnight, according to the capital's mayor, Sergey Sobyanin. Writing on Telegram, Sobyanin reported that approximately 139 drones were intercepted in total through the night and into Monday morning, with emergency service personnel deployed to areas where debris landed. This aerial assault followed recent Ukrainian strikes targeting a major Russian petrochemical facility, an oil refinery, and a military manufacturing site.

The drone interceptions occurred just days before a scheduled summit in Shenzhen, China, where Russian President Vladimir Putin is set to meet with U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. China verified that Xi will host the talks on November 19 on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, though Beijing did not release an agenda.

U.S. officials indicated that while President Trump intends to address nuclear arms reduction and the conflict involving Iran during the trilateral discussions, the nearly five-year war between Russia and Ukraine is not expected to be a topic. Instead, Washington is pursuing separate diplomatic negotiations involving Kyiv and Moscow to resolve the conflict. Meanwhile, German President Frank-German President Frank-Frank-Frank-Steinmeier noted that President Xi recently expressed irritation regarding suggestions to include the Ukraine war in the trilateral format, stressing it is a European conflict requiring European participation.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky expressed concern that the upcoming Shenzhen meeting could mirror the 1945 Yalta conference, potentially leading major powers to negotiate spheres of influence without smaller nations present at the negotiating table.

stories.title: ICC announces 2028-2031 tournament hosts as India, England, Australia, and New Zealand sweep events
stories.summary:
The International Cricket Council released its schedule for the 2028-2035 cycle, revealing that India, England, Australia, and New Zealand will host all marquee events scheduled between 2028 and 2031. Venues for matches taking place from 2032 to 2035 will be determined at a later date. Notably, Pakistan—which successfully hosted an eight-tier Champions Trophy tournament last year—was not awarded any hosting duties for the upcoming cycle.

Under the newly approved schedule, Australia and New Zealand will co-host the 2028 T20 World Cup. India will host the 2029 ICC Champions Trophy and jointly organize the 2031 ICC World Cup alongside Bangladesh. England is set to hold the ICC Test Championship final in both 2029 and 2030, and will also share hosting duties for the 2030 T20 World Cup with Ireland and Scotland. The governing body stated that these choices aim to expand opportunities for full and associate members while strengthening qualification pathways.

In addition to tournament hosts, the ICC outlined various qualification structures. The 2027 Men’s World Cup Qualifier in February and March will feature 10 teams divided into two groups of five, culminating in semi-finals and a final. A separate 16-team Global Qualifier in early 2028 will determine eight direct participants for the 2028 Men’s T20 World Cup. For the women's pathway, the Netherlands and Scotland will join eight regional qualifiers in a global tournament to secure the final two spots for the 2028 ICC Women’s T20 World Cup.

Furthermore, host nations and dates were finalized for the last qualification phase for cricket's return to the Olympics at the Los Angeles 2028 Games. The men’s qualifier will take place from February 5 to 13, 2028, in Bangladesh, while the women’s event is scheduled from February 26 to March 5, 2028, in the United States. Each tournament will comprise eight teams competing for a single qualification berth.

stories.title: Karachi water shortages persist despite maintenance completion at Dhabeji pumping station
stories.summary:
Residents in multiple neighborhoods across Karachi experienced water shortages for a third consecutive day on Sunday, even though the Karachi Water and Sewerage Corporation announced the completion of annual maintenance work at the Dhabeji pumping station. The utility previously warned that maintenance activities starting November 13 would result in a daily supply shortfall of roughly 130 million gallons. On Sunday, officials confirmed that all 21 pumps at Dhabeji were fully operational and that overall city supply had been restored.

According to the utility's statement, technical tasks such as valve installations and pipeline repairs were successfully concluded. Water distribution to impacted sectors, including Landhi, Korangi, Malir, and Shah Faisal towns, was reportedly being gradually normalized. However, the agency's announcement did not specify a exact timeline for when full service would resume for all affected consumers.

A KWSC spokesperson detailed that various improvements were executed during the operation to boost the efficiency and stability of the water network. These measures included installing a new 60-inch-diameter valve at Dhabeji, carrying out repairs across pump houses at the Pipri station, replacing approximately 150 feet of water pipeline along Shahrah-i-Bhutto, and fixing a leakage in the Haleji conduit.

stories.title: Karachi Residents Alarmed as Public Parks and Grounds Go Commercial
stories.summary:
In Karachi, the rising commercialisation of public parks and playgrounds by the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation and Town Municipal Corporations has sparked serious concerns. Local residents and youth groups point out that facilities meant for community recreation are increasingly controlled by private operators who charge heavy fees for activities like cricket, futsal, and padel. This shift limits access for children and low-income families.

Across multiple districts, grounds have been outsourced to private entities. In Korangi, venues like the Rashid Latif Cricket Academy and Eidgah Ground charge thousands for matches, with night bookings running even higher due to generator costs. Similar commercial rates apply at Umer Sharif Park in the South District, Hill Park in the East, Annu Bhai Cricket Ground in Central, and Baloch Mujahid Football Ground in Malir. Critics argue that these fees exclude ordinary citizens and contrast sharply with poorly maintained free areas.

Local representatives and officials defend the outsourcing model. Korangi Town Chairman Naeem Sheikh stated that partial leasing helps maintain grounds in better condition, while noting that children are barred from hardball matches to prevent injuries. A KMC spokesperson explained that the corporation does not set prices and that private contractors charge based on market rates to cover maintenance and operational expenses.

Residents and former athletes have strongly condemned the trend, urging municipal authorities to fund upkeep directly rather than relying on private profiting. They argue that accessible public spaces are vital for keeping young people engaged in healthy activities and away from social issues like drug addiction.

stories.title: Pakistan Ties Afghan Cooperation to Counter-Terrorism Action at ECO Summit
stories.summary:
Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar stated that regional stability and meaningful cooperation with Afghanistan depend on Afghan authorities addressing cross-border security and terrorism concerns. Speaking at the Economic Cooperation Organisation Council of Ministers meeting in Islamabad, Dar emphasized that a peaceful and integrated Afghanistan would immensely benefit regional trade and transit.

Dar highlighted that mutual trust and the strict fulfillment of international obligations are foundational for long-term economic partnerships. The two-day ministerial gathering follows a senior officials meeting chaired by Foreign Secretary Ambassador Asim Iftikhar Ahmad, which finalized the draft Islamabad Communiqué. Member states also reviewed the ECO Secretariat's annual activities and discussed financial and administrative improvements.

Under the chairmanship of Pakistan for 2026-27, participating leaders are focusing on the theme 'Reviving Regionalism for a Resilient ECO'. A key agenda item for Central Asian leaders during the summit is the discussion and adoption of ECO Vision 2035, a ten-year strategic framework designed to boost regional connectivity and sustainable growth.

The Economic Cooperation Organization currently includes Pakistan, Afghanistan, Azerbaijan, Tajikistan, Iran, Turkiye, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, the Kyrgyz Republic, and Uzbekistan. Discussions at the capital continue to center on deepening regional integration, enhancing trade routes, and establishing robust security frameworks to ensure lasting economic progress.

stories.title: Fauji Foods Names Waseem Haider as New Acting Chief Executive
stories.summary:
Fauji Foods Limited has officially announced the appointment of Waseem Haider as its acting Chief Executive Officer, taking effect on November 15, 2026. The publicly listed food and dairy enterprise disclosed the leadership change in a formal notice submitted to the Pakistan Stock Exchange on Monday.

Haider steps into the role to replace outgoing CEO Usman Zaheer Ahmad. Prior to this appointment, Waseem Haider had been serving as the Chief Financial Officer of Fauji Foods since June 2022. He is a fellow member of CIMA UK and boasts more than 27 years of extensive financial experience, having worked with prominent blue-chip companies in Pakistan and internationally across the MENA and Oceania regions.

The transition follows the departure of Usman Zaheer Ahmad, who resigned from his position as CEO of Fauji Foods on September 18, 2026, before moving on to lead FrieslandCampina Engro Pakistan Limited later that month.

Originally founded in 1966 as Noon Pakistan Limited, the company was acquired by the Fauji Foundation and Fauji Fertiliser in 2015 and subsequently rebranded as Fauji Foods Limited. Operating as a subsidiary of Fauji Fertilizer Bin Qasim Limited within the larger Fauji Group established in 1954, the company specializes in processing and marketing toned milk, milk powder, fruit juices, and value-added dairy items including cheese, butter, and cream.

stories.title: Indonesian President Apologizes to Neighbors Over Toxic Wildfire Haze
stories.summary:
Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto issued a formal apology to Malaysia and Singapore regarding the severe transboundary haze caused by extensive domestic wildfires. Addressing fellow leaders at an Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit in Manila, Prabowo expressed regret for the suffering inflicted upon neighboring populations, despite asserting that Jakarta had done its utmost to combat the blazes.

The widespread fires, centered across Borneo, Sumatra, and Papua, have scorched 2.88 million hectares of land in 2026. This ongoing environmental crisis has generated toxic air pollution that sickened hundreds of thousands locally and drifted across national borders. Researchers attribute the severity of this year's fire season to a potent El Nino phenomenon, climate change, deforestation, and peatland drainage.

In response to the crisis, Prabowo noted that Indonesian authorities deployed 71,000 personnel to control the flames, though the mission has resulted in the loss of 16 firefighters and two helicopters. Furthermore, the government has revoked land concessions from 17 corporations linked to the blazes, with 26 additional companies currently under active investigation.

The environmental disaster has also taken a heavy human toll domestically, with pollution-related conditions responsible for 3,560 deaths in Indonesia during the month of September alone. The summit highlights ongoing regional challenges in addressing transboundary environmental degradation and climate-induced disasters.

stories.title: Jensen Huang Weighs Nvidia Comeback Amid Industry Scandal and Crisis
stories.summary:
Former Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang is reportedly weighing a potential return to the company he helped build, having held discussions with close confidants about making a comeback. According to sources familiar with the situation, a group of allies is organizing a Silicon Valley "war room" to lobby for Huang's reinstatement and seek backing from the White House. This move follows Huang's sudden departure on Thursday after disclosures concerning extramarital relationships, including an association with a suspected Chinese spy that sparked worries regarding the export of high-end artificial intelligence chips to China.

The unexpected exit has plunged the prominent chip manufacturer into severe turmoil, sending ripples through the broader artificial intelligence sector that Huang previously supported financially. Prior to his resignation, Nvidia's board had reportedly engaged British chipmaker Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas to explore possible successor options. Meanwhile, the company continues to be led under its existing executive structure, featuring Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress, who has served in the role since joining the firm in September 2013 and steering its financial growth alongside Huang.

Nvidia has not yet issued an immediate statement in response to inquiries regarding the potential leadership shift outside normal business hours. The ongoing uncertainty surrounds a critical period for the company, which has seen its market valuation fluctuate significantly amid growing investor scrutiny. The brewing controversy adds to broader international tensions, unfolding concurrently with military developments in Eastern Europe where Russian authorities intercepted numerous drones over Moscow ahead of an upcoming global summit.

Industry observers note that any potential comeback by Huang would require substantial alignment among key technology stakeholders and political figures. While supporters maintain that major industry figures outside frontier laboratories remain deeply supportive of his leadership, the path forward remains highly complex. The unfolding developments will likely continue to heavily impact Nvidia's strategic trajectory and governance as the board and allies navigate the fallout from the recent executive crisis.

stories.title: امریکہ، روس اور چین کے سربراہان کی ممکنہ سہ فریقی ملاقات، یورپ میں تشویش کی لہر
stories.summary:
امریکہ، روس اور چین کے سربراہان کی پہلی سہ فریقی ملاقات کی تیاریاں جاری ہیں، جس نے یورپ اور بالخصوص یوکرین میں شدید تشویش پیدا کر دی ہے۔ 18 اور 19 نومبر کو ایشیا پیسیفک اقتصادی تعاون (ایپک) کے سربراہی اجلاس کے دوران روس کے صدر ولادیمیر پوتن، امریکی صدر ڈونلڈ ٹرمپ اور چینی صدر شی جن پنگ کی چین کے شہر شینژن میں ملاقات متوقع ہے۔ وائٹ ہاؤس کی ترجمان اولیویا ویلز نے جمعے کو اس ملاقات کی تصدیق کی تھی۔ اس ممکنہ ملاقات نے سنہ 1945 کی تاریخی یالٹا کانفرنس کی یاد تازہ کر دی ہے، جہاں دوسری عالمی جنگ کے دوران بڑی طاقتوں کے رہنماؤں نے دنیا کی نئی ترتیب اور اثر و رسوخ کے حصے طے کیے تھے۔

یوکرین کے صدر ولادیمیر زیلنسکی نے خدشہ ظاہر کیا ہے کہ اس ملاقات کا مقصد دنیا کو تقسیم کرنا اور چھوٹے ممالک کے مفادات کو نظرانداز کرنا ہو سکتا ہے۔ دوسری طرف جرمن چانسلر فریڈرک مرز کا کہنا ہے کہ یوکرین میں جنگ کے خاتمے اور سکیورٹی انتظامات سے متعلق کسی بھی بات چیت میں یورپ کی شمولیت ناگزیر ہے۔ امریکی اخبار ’وال سٹریٹ جنرل‘ کے مطابق پوتن کا مقصد یوکرین جنگ کو روس کے حق میں ختم کرنے کے لیے حمایت حاصل کرنا ہے۔ تاہم، امریکی صدر ڈونلڈ ٹرمپ نے اس ملاقات میں یوکرین کے معاملے پر بات ہونے کی تردید کرتے ہوئے کہا ہے کہ تینوں رہنما جوہری ہتھیاروں میں کمی پر بات کر سکتے ہیں۔

واشنگٹن کی امریکن یونیورسٹی کے ایسوسی ایٹ پروفیسر جوزف ٹوریگین کا کہنا ہے کہ ٹرمپ اس ملاقات کا سہرا اپنے سر باندھ کر عالمی امن کے لیے اہم کردار ادا کرنے کا دعویٰ کرنا چاہتے ہیں۔ دوسری جانب، روس کا مقصد یورپ کو نظرانداز کر کے یہ ثابت کرنا ہے کہ وہ عالمی سطح پر تنہا نہیں ہے۔ تاہم، چین کے لیے اس ملاقات کے فوائد اتنے واضح نہیں ہیں کیونکہ تاریخی یالٹا کانفرنس کے تلخ تجربات کی وجہ سے بیجنگ نہیں چاہتا کہ وہ کسی ایسی بات چیت کا حصہ بنے جہاں یوکرین کے معاملے پر یورپ کو مکمل طور پر نظرانداز کیا جائے، اور نہ ہی چین جوہری ہتھیاروں کے مذاکرات کے حوالے سے زیادہ پُرامید ہے۔

stories.title: Pakistan Stock Exchange Surges Over 1,000 Points in Early Trading
stories.summary:
The Pakistan Stock Exchange initiated the trading week with strong upward momentum as the benchmark KSE-100 Index surged past the 1,000-point threshold during Monday's opening session. By 9:40 am, the index stood at 178,936.99, reflecting an increase of 1,063.12 points or 0.60%. Widespread buying activity was observed across multiple vital sectors, encompassing automobile assemblers, commercial banks, cement manufacturers, oil and gas exploration firms, oil marketing companies, and power generation units. Major market-heavy stocks, including HUBCO, MARI, OGDC, POL, PPL, HBL, MEBL, NBP, and UBL, all traded positively during the morning hours. This latest surge builds upon the market's previous weekly performance, where the KSE-100 Index advanced by 3,987.19 points or 2.3% to settle at 177,873.88 points. Investor sentiment during that preceding period was notably bolstered by declining international oil prices and robust inflows of workers' remittances into the country. In contrast to Pakistan's positive market opening, Asian shares experienced a downturn on Monday following a turbulent week globally. International markets have been reacting to major developments, including the abrupt departure of Jensen Huang as the chief executive of Nvidia. Investors globally are now looking toward upcoming corporate earnings and initial public offerings, such as Anthropic's IPO, to gauge the ongoing strength of the artificial intelligence-driven bull market.
Additionally, international markets are closely monitoring upcoming geopolitical events, including a scheduled meeting between US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen. Investors are also preparing for upcoming US Federal Reserve policy minutes and commentary regarding potential interest rate trajectories. Meanwhile, Nvidia's market capitalization has experienced significant declines following Huang's exit, leaving market analysts waiting to see if the chipmaker maintains its optimistic financial outlook under new leadership.

stories.title: Pakistani Government Advances Plans for a Separate Islamabad Legislative Assembly
stories.summary:
Authorities in Pakistan are actively intensifying efforts to establish an independent legislative assembly for the capital city of Islamabad. Under current proposals, the new provincial-style government would be governed by a designated assembly headed by an elected mayor or chief minister. This initiative stems from recommendations previously finalized by a high-profile committee led by Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, which were subsequently submitted to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif for review.

The initial framework envisioned an Islamabad Assembly consisting of 27 members, operating through the devolution of administrative powers from the federal government to the Islamabad Capital Territory as a distinct federating unit. Recent discussions have further introduced potential boundary expansions, with emerging reports suggesting that regions such as Haripur, Murree, and parts of Rawalpindi might potentially be integrated into Islamabad. However, a senior government official clarified that while a separate legislative assembly is definite, any incorporation of external areas remains under discussion and is not yet finalized.

This legislative push coincides with persistent delays surrounding local government elections within the capital. Local polls have faced postponement at least five times over the past four years, with authorities consistently citing ongoing legislative efforts to build a more robust administrative system. Although elections had been most recently scheduled for December 20, the Islamabad High Court suspended the schedule following a petition challenging the legal standing of the existing constituency delimitation.

The broader debate over administrative restructuring in Islamabad highlights the federal government's ongoing efforts to reform local governance structures despite recurring legal and political hurdles. While discussions regarding territorial expansion and provincial-style autonomy continue among policymakers, the precise implementation mechanism and final boundaries remain subject to further deliberation and legislative approval.

stories.title: Riyadh Begins Construction on Massive Expo Station for Metro Network
stories.summary:
The Royal Commission for Riyadh City has officially initiated construction on the Riyadh Metro's Expo Station, accompanied by the release of its detailed architectural plans. Covering a footprint of approximately 70,000 square metres, the massive transport hub is engineered to handle up to 19,000 passengers every hour. The project forms a core component of the commission's broader strategy to upgrade Riyadh's public transit infrastructure to support rapid population growth and ongoing urban expansion.

Designed to serve visitors traveling to Expo 2030 Riyadh, the station will also function as a permanent fixture within the city's broader metro system once the global exhibition concludes. Positioned strategically along the Yellow Line connecting directly to King Khalid International Airport, the station extends across King Salman Road. It is intended to anchor a landscaped green corridor linking the Expo site on the eastern side with forthcoming urban development zones located to the west.

The architectural concept draws inspiration from local geographical features, specifically regional valleys and acacia trees, highlighted by a 134-metre-diameter steel dome resting on eight branching columns. Emphasizing environmental sustainability, the facility will incorporate roughly 44,000 square metres of green space alongside solar power systems designed to supply about a quarter of the station's overall energy needs. The Royal Commission for Riyadh City aims to complete the construction ahead of the Expo's official opening to guarantee full operational readiness.

To manage potential disruption during the building phase, authorities have formulated a comprehensive traffic management strategy in partnership with relevant agencies. This plan establishes alternative transit routes to keep traffic flowing smoothly and protect neighboring residential communities from congestion while maintaining steady accessibility throughout the construction timeline.

stories.title: China’s First 10-Ton Electric Commercial Aircraft Completes Piloted Flight
stories.summary:
China has achieved a milestone in aviation as its independently developed CE-25A electric commercial aircraft completed its first piloted test flight on Saturday in Binzhou, Shandong province. The maiden crewed flight carried two pilots and a flight-test engineer, with the aircraft operating normally and meeting all performance expectations, according to the Commercial Aircraft Corporation of China (COMAC). This event follows the aircraft's initial unmanned autonomous flight on February 2, after which it underwent 19 unmanned autonomous flight validations.

The CE-25A is COMAC's inaugural electric commercial model, designed primarily for intercity routes. It accommodates 19 passengers and features a maximum takeoff weight of 10 metric tons, alongside a cruising speed of 300 kilometers per hour, a cruising altitude of 2,400 meters, and a range of 400 kilometers. Rather than relying on traditional turbofan or turboprop engines, the aircraft is powered by a distributed electric propulsion system comprising 10 electric ducted fans mounted across the top of its wings. This innovative configuration is intended to minimize noise and facilitate takeoffs and landings on shorter runways.

The aircraft was developed through a collaborative effort involving COMAC, Chinese battery manufacturer CATL, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, and other partners. Following these successful flight tests, the Civil Aviation Administration of China (CAAC) has formally accepted COMAC's type certificate application under transport-category regulations, initiating the rigorous inspection process necessary before the aircraft can enter commercial passenger service.

stories.title: Nvidia Shares Plunge Following Controversies Surrounding CEO Jensen Huang
stories.summary:
Nvidia experienced a dramatic market downturn after its shares dropped 18 percent over five trading sessions, erasing roughly $913 billion from its market valuation. The financial drop coincided with growing scrutiny over long-time co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang, whose personal conduct has ignited intense corporate governance debates. Huang publicly acknowledged an extramarital relationship following reports that the individual involved, Chinese business executive Alice Huang, was suspected by American intelligence officials of acting on behalf of Beijing. Furthermore, allegations regarding a second relationship involving a senior Nvidia executive who reported directly to Huang have surfaced, compounding concerns regarding leadership accountability and potential conflicts of interest.

While US intelligence officials reportedly believed Alice Huang may have been recruited by Chinese intelligence, Beijing has dismissed these allegations as groundless, and there are no established public findings that she engaged in espionage, that Jensen Huang knowingly assisted foreign intelligence operations, or that sensitive information was compromised. Nevertheless, Nvidia's board launched an independent investigation, and Huang has since resigned. This controversy underscores the immense vulnerability that arises when a company's corporate identity and global success are inextricably linked to a single charismatic founder.

Because Nvidia occupies a critical role in artificial intelligence leadership, semiconductor geopolitics, and American national security policy, Huang's personal visibility and his involvement in high-level discussions between Washington and Beijing linked corporate fortunes directly to national interests. Financial analysts and corporate governance experts note that this crisis serves as a cautionary tale for businesses worldwide, including in Pakistan, where companies frequently rely heavily on powerful, visible personalities rather than distributing leadership across a robust C-suite team. Ultimately, the situation highlights the necessity for independent board oversight, genuine delegation of responsibility, and credible succession planning to ensure institutions can maintain stakeholder confidence independently of their founders.

stories.title: Karachi Police Arrest Two Suspects Transporting Hashish via Rickshaw
stories.summary:
Police in Karachi arrested two individuals allegedly involved in narcotics trafficking during an intelligence-led operation in Madina Colony, Scheme 33, according to reports on Monday. SSP East Zubair Nazir Sheikh stated that Sachal police personnel intercepted the suspects, identified as Muhammad Amin and Idris, who were utilizing a motorized rickshaw to distribute illegal substances across various neighborhoods in the city. 

During the raid, law enforcement authorities recovered more than 28 kilograms of hashish from the vehicle. In addition to the narcotics, officers seized mobile phones and a sum of cash believed to be direct proceeds generated from illicit drug sales. The operation represents another enforcement action by local police against urban drug supply networks operating within the commercial hub.

This arrest follows a prior operation conducted on January 29 near Tipu Sultan Road by officials from the Ferozabad police station. In that raid, police dismantled a four-member racket supplying synthetic ice drugs, heroin, charas, and antidotes to students. That earlier operation resulted in the seizure of a substantial quantity of ice powder alongside two motorcycles, seven mobile phones, and other assets, with the detained suspects identified as Gul Ameer, Sadam Hussain, Naim, and Hazrat Gul, all originally from Quetta and residing in Karachi's Sohrab Goth area.

stories.title: Global Oil Markets Pivot From Shortage Fears to Anticipated Surplus
stories.summary:
Oil markets have experienced a dramatic reversal in sentiment, shifting concerns away from severe shortages toward a looming global surplus. Following the Republican setback in mid-term elections and subsequent cooling of Middle East hostilities—highlighted by US President Donald Trump declaring the conflict with Iran "effectively over"—crude prices have fallen sharply. Brent crude for January delivery settled at $95.84 per barrel on Friday, November 13, while West Texas Intermediate (WTI) settled at December delivery of $88.56 per barrel. This represents a steep decline from peaks of $126 per barrel in April, continuing consecutive weeks of heavy price drops.

The International Energy Agency (IEA) reported that global oil supplies outstripped demand by nearly 2 million barrels per day (bpd) in October, driven by Gulf exports recovering much faster than worldwide demand. The IEA projects global oil supply to average 105 million bpd in the final quarter of the year, outstripping demand forecasts by 1.7 million bpd. To manage this shifting landscape, IEA members are accelerating the release of 71 million barrels of emergency stockpiles by the end of February 2027. Concurrently, OPEC+ reported a surge in October production to an average of 41.23 million bpd, driven largely by Saudi Arabia restoring output to pre-war levels of 10.56 million bpd and rising production in Iraq and Russia, often utilizing maritime workarounds to bypass ongoing regional shipping disruptions.

Simultaneously, global demand growth concerns are weighing on the market. While OPEC maintains steady demand projections, the IEA forecasts a 2.68 million bpd fall in global oil demand for the year, citing high prices, increasing vehicle electrification, and improved fuel efficiency. The US Energy Information Administration (EIA) similarly noted that global liquid fuels consumption will drop by 2 million bpd in 2026, driven largely by reduced economic activity and lower consumption in China and the Middle East. Nevertheless, geopolitical risks persist, as tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and infrastructure strikes by the Houthis in Saudi Arabia continue to present intermittent supply threats despite the overarching market shift toward a glut.

stories.title: Punjab Government Launches Second Phase of Livestock Card Distribution
stories.summary:
The Punjab government has officially commenced the distribution of the second instalment of financial assistance through the Livestock Card Scheme. Initiated on November 15, 2026, the program is managed by the Punjab Livestock and Dairy Development Department to aid local livestock keepers.

Registered beneficiaries can use these specialized cards to acquire vital animal care supplies, such as concentrated feed known as Wanda, silage, and animal feed through approved retail partners and registered dealers. To support participants, the provincial administration has also introduced a round-the-clock helpline via phone number 08000-9211 to answer questions and offer assistance regarding the initiative.

This welfare effort is designed to boost animal nutrition, assist agricultural workers, and reinforce the regional livestock economy. Officials noted that the inaugural phase achieved a 96 percent loan recovery rate, with 23,312 cards printed and handed out throughout the province.

During the initial rollout, 1,739 farmers completed upward of 70,000 purchases. Expenditures included 892.6 million rupees spent on Wanda, 87 million rupees on silage, and 20 million rupees dedicated to mineral mixtures. Additionally, female involvement expanded significantly, as the count of participating women livestock farmers grew from 90 to 1,107.

stories.title: Punjab Sugar Mills Defy Crushing Orders Over Support Price Dispute
stories.summary:
The majority of sugar production facilities across Punjab have failed to commence sugarcane crushing activities, ignoring an official provincial mandate requiring operations to begin by mid-November. According to a representative of the Pakistan Sugar Mills Association, only Ramzan Sugar Mills adhered to the directive issued by the Punjab Food Safety and Consumer Protection Department on behalf of the governor.

The initial order instructed processing plants to start purchasing crops and launch operations within a 24-hour window, while charging local deputy commissioners with enforcing compliance. In response to the standoff, both the association's northern zone representatives and various farming coalitions organized press conferences to voice their respective positions on the delayed harvest season.

Grower leaders stated that the provincial decree proved ineffective as mills remained shut in Punjab and operations stalled in Sindh. Farmers argue that the inaction is inflicting monetary damages amid rising expenses for di-ammonium phosphate fertiliser, prompting demands for the establishment of a fixed support price and an appeal for intervention by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.

Official figures indicate that sugarcane cultivation spans 2.452 million acres in Punjab this year, marking a 16 percent expansion compared to the prior season. Earlier, Minister for National Food Security and Research Rana Tanveer Hussain chaired a consultation where the Sugar Advisory Board fixed November 15 for nationwide operations to protect growers from exploitation and guarantee prior payment of dues.

stories.title: افغانستان کے پہاڑوں میں چھپے قدرتی معدنی وسائل کی مالیت 30 کھرب ڈالر سے زائد
stories.summary:
افغانستان میں تیل، گیس، دھاتوں اور دیگر معدنی وسائل کی کل مالیت 30 کھرب ڈالر یعنی 840 کھرب پاکستانی روپے سے زائد بتائی گئی ہے۔ اگرچہ ملک طویل عرصے سے معاشی مشکلات کا شکار ہے، لیکن اس کے زیر زمین موجود یہ وسیع ذخائر اس بات کی نشاندہی کرتے ہیں کہ اگر یہ وسائل بروئے کار لائے جائیں تو ملک کو تقریباً 300 سال تک کسی غیر ملکی اقتصادی امداد کی ضرورت نہیں پڑے گی۔ افغانستان میں ان معدنی ذخائر پر سب سے پہلے بڑے پیمانے پر تحقیق سابق سوویت یونین کے دور میں کی گئی تھی، جس کے بعد 2007 اور 2011 میں بھی امریکی اور افغان جیولوجیکل سروے کے ذریعے مختلف مطالعے کیے گئے۔

رپورٹ کے مطابق افغانستان کے قدرتی وسائل کو بنیادی دھاتوں اور دیگر حصوں میں تقسیم کیا گیا ہے، جن کی مالیت 10 کھرب ڈالر سے زیادہ ہے۔ بدخشاں اور تخار کے علاقوں میں سونے کے اہم ذخائر موجود ہیں، جہاں تخار کی ’چا آب‘ کان کا ٹھیکہ دو کمپنیوں کو دیا گیا ہے اور بدخشاں سے ہر ماہ کئی ٹن سونا نکالا جا رہا ہے۔ اس کے علاوہ، افغانستان میں خطے کے سب سے بڑے لوہے کے ذخائر پائے جاتے ہیں جن کی مقدار تقریباً تین ارب ٹن ہے اور بامیان، پنجشیر، ہرات سمیت مختلف صوبوں میں ان کی کانیں موجود ہیں۔ طالبان حکومت نے ہرات کے غوریان علاقے میں لوہے کے چار بلاکس کے ٹھیکے بھی دیے ہیں جن کی مالیت 2.5 ارب ڈالر ہے۔

افغانستان کے پاس تانبے کے بھی دنیا کے بڑے ذخائر موجود ہیں جن کا تخمینہ چھ کروڑ ٹن تک لگایا گیا ہے اور ان کی مالیت 720 ارب ڈالر ہو سکتی ہے۔ لوگر کی ’آئینک‘ کان اس سلسلے میں سب سے اہم ہے، جسے حال ہی میں 30 سال کے لیے ایک نجی کمپنی کو لیز پر دیا گیا ہے۔ زابل، قندھار اور بغلان میں ایلومینیم کے ذخائر کی مالیت 30 ارب ڈالر سے زیادہ ہے، جبکہ قندھار اور دیگر اضلاع میں سیسہ، زنک، ٹن، ٹنگسٹن اور پارے کے ذخائر بھی پائے جاتے ہیں جن کے بعض کانوں کے ٹھیکے بھی دیے جا چکے ہیں۔

stories.title: حوثیوں کے حملے کا دعویٰ، سعودی عرب میں ڈرون روکنے کی اطلاعات
stories.summary: یمن کے حوثی گروپ انصار اللہ نے اتوار کی شام دعویٰ کیا ہے کہ اس نے سعودی دارالحکومت ریاض میں واقع شاہ خالد انٹرنیشنل ایئرپورٹ اور ایسٹ ویسٹ پائپ لائن کو دو بیلسٹک میزائلوں سے نشانہ بنایا ہے۔ حوثی فوج کے ترجمان یحییٰ سریع کے مطابق، گروپ نے ریاض کے علاقے میں اس آئل پائپ لائن کے پمپنگ اسٹیشن نمبر پانچ اور چھ پر بھی دو ڈرون حملے کیے۔ دوسری جانب، سعودی زیر قیادت اتحاد کے ترجمان ترکی المالکی نے بتایا کہ فضائی دفاعی نظام نے ریاض کی جانب داغے گئے دو بیلسٹک میزائلوں کو فضا میں ہی تباہ کر دیا۔ اتحادی افواج نے حوثیوں پر مکہ اور مدینہ کی جانب آنے والے تین ڈرونز کو تباہ کرنے اور مکہ کو نشانہ بنانے کی کوشش کا الزام بھی عائد کیا، جسے حوثی ترجمان نے جھوٹا اور من گھڑت قرار دے کر مسترد کر دیا۔ اس دوران، یمنی حکومتی فورسز نے باب المندب آبنائے کے قریب ذباب ایئرپورٹ اور دیگر علاقوں سے انخلا کا اعلان کیا ہے تاکہ عدن کے دفاع پر توجہ دی جا سکے۔ اس پیش رفت سے بحیرہ احمر کے داخلی راستے کے قریب ساحلی علاقوں پر حوثیوں کی پیش قدمی کے بعد سعودی تیل برآمدات پر دباؤ بڑھ گیا ہے۔ ان تمام کشیدگیوں کے تناظر میں خطے میں سکیورٹی کی صورتحال مزید پیچیدہ ہوتی جا رہی ہے اور دونوں اطراف سے حملوں اور دعوؤں کا سلسلہ جاری ہے۔

stories.title: حکومت نے نیکٹا سے نیشنل انٹیلیجنس فیوژن اینڈ تھریٹ اسیسمنٹ سینٹر واپس لے لیا
stories.summary: پاکستانی حکومت نے نیشنل کاؤنٹر ٹیرارزم اتھارٹی سے نیشنل انٹیلیجنس فیوژن اینڈ تھریٹ اسیسمنٹ سینٹر یعنی نفٹاک واپس لے لیا ہے۔ محسن نقوی کے ماتحت وزارت داخلہ اب اس سینٹر کے کام کا براہ راست معائنہ کرے گی، جس کے بعد نیکٹا کے قانونی مینڈیٹ کا ایک اہم حصہ متاثر ہونے کا خدشہ ظاہر کیا جا رہا ہے۔ ستمبر کے پہلے ہفتے میں میجر جنرل فیصل نصیر کو تین برس کے لیے نیکٹا کا پہلا فوجی نیشنل کوآرڈینیٹر مقرر کیا گیا تھا۔ وزارت داخلہ کے حکام کے مطابق اس تنظیمی تبدیلی کا مقصد انٹیلیجنس رابطہ کاری اور معلومات کے تبادلے کے نظام کو زیادہ مؤثر بنانا ہے، اور اس ماڈل کو صوبوں تک بھی بڑھا دیا گیا ہے۔ دوسری جانب، نیکٹا کے سابق سربراہان اور ماہرین کا کہنا ہے کہ اس علیحدگی کے بعد نیکٹا کا ادارہ عملاً ایک ریسرچ ونگ یا تھنک ٹینک کی حد تک محدود ہو گیا ہے۔ سابق سربراہ طارق پرویز نے خدشہ ظاہر کیا کہ اس تبدیلی اور فوجی پس منظر کے حامل افسر کی تقرری سے آزادانہ تھریٹ اسیسمنٹ متاثر ہو سکتی ہے اور سویلین و فوجی توازن میں فرق آ سکتا ہے۔ سابق سربراہان کے مطابق اس فیصلے سے پہلے ان سے کوئی مشاورت نہیں کی گئی اور اس کی وجوہات یا نئے روڈ میپ کے حوالے سے بھی ابہام پایا جاتا ہے۔ وزیر مملکت برائے داخلہ طلال چوہدری نے تصدیق کی ہے کہ یہ وزارت کے اندرونی امور اور انتظامی بہتری کا معمول کا عمل ہے جس سے متعلق ابہام جلد ختم ہو جائے گا۔

stories.title: PTI Senator Khurram Zeeshan Announces Resignation From Upper House
stories.summary:
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Senator Khurram Zeeshan has announced his resignation from his seat in the upper house of the parliament and from his party position. Zeeshan stated that he planned to submit his resignation directly to the party leadership and would personally appear before the Chairman Senate to fulfill all required legal formalities if necessary.

Addressing the role of his parliamentary vote, Zeeshan noted that the party leadership must decide whether his vote remains essential for PTI founder Imran Khan. He emphasized that if his vote is needed, the party should reject his resignation because he views his vote as a trust entrusted to him by the PTI founder.

Looking toward his political future, Zeeshan confirmed he has no intention of contesting any upcoming elections, including future Senate races. However, he pledged to maintain his support for the PTI founder by continuing his political struggle as an ordinary party worker and a citizen of Pakistan.

In addition to his political announcement, Zeeshan addressed accusations concerning gold mining, vowing to pursue legal action to the fullest extent against individuals making such allegations. He stated that formal legal notices would be dispatched to the responsible parties within the next few days.

stories.title: Exploring the History and Impact of Intelligence Honeytraps Throughout Time
stories.summary:
The historical use of intelligence honeytraps spans centuries, ranging from ancient biblical accounts to modern corporate espionage concerns. This classic tactic involves deploying romantic or personal relationships to extract sensitive information or influence key targets for strategic advantage.

Early examples include the biblical story of Samson and Delilah, where Delilah uncovered the secret to Samson's legendary strength. Later, during the world wars and the Cold War, honeytraps became a widespread intelligence-gathering tool utilized by various nations and organizations.

Notable historical instances involve individuals such as British author Roald Dahl, who acted as a Romeo spy in American high society during the early 1940s to garner support for Allied war efforts. Similarly, the East German Stasi operated a dedicated department of male spies known as Juliets to target vulnerable secretaries and assistants working in Western offices.

Other historical cases include the KGB's entrapment of British civil servant John Vassal in Moscow during the 1950s, as well as the twenty-year affair between French diplomat Bernard Boursicort and Chinese opera singer Shi Pei Pu, who was revealed to be a man after their arrest in 1983. These historical operations highlight how personal vulnerabilities have continuously been exploited to acquire classified information.

stories.title: Jensen Huang Considers Nvidia Return Following Resignation Over Alleged Spy Scandal
stories.summary:
Former Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang is reportedly considering a comeback and has discussed a potential return with close confidants and tech allies. Huang stepped down from his position on Thursday following revelations regarding extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy.

According to reports from the Financial Times, a supporter stated that a war room of Silicon Valley executives is being assembled to lobby for Huang's reinstatement and seek support from the White House. The ally noted that industry leaders outside the frontier labs strongly support Huang, and these efforts reportedly carry the former CEO's backing.

The scandal surrounding Huang's departure has plunged the prominent chipmaker into crisis, sending shockwaves through the artificial intelligence industry that he helped finance. The controversy has additionally raised questions regarding the export of Nvidia's advanced artificial intelligence computer chips to China, a market linked to $7.5 billion in shipments.

Before Huang's discussions of a potential return emerged, the Financial Times reported that Nvidia's board of directors had already approached Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas while searching for a potential successor. Nvidia did not immediately respond to requests for comment outside of regular business hours.

stories.title: Indus Waters Treaty in Abeyance Strains India-Pakistan Relations
stories.summary:
The 1960 Indus Waters Treaty, historically known as a durable water-sharing agreement between India and Pakistan, has faced severe disruption after India placed the pact in abeyance. This decision reflects a strategic shift as climate change, glacial retreat, erratic monsoons, and droughts make water availability unpredictable in the Himalayan cryosphere. The World Resources Institute warns that South Asia faces rising baseline water stress, making water a key factor in national security and pushing states toward unilateral actions.

For Pakistan, whose agrarian economy depends heavily on the Indus basin for food security and rural livelihoods, India's construction of storage dams along the Chenab River—such as the Chenab-Beas link tunnel and the Salal sediment bypass—poses an existential threat. These projects increase India's ability to control and divert water flows, raising concerns about cumulative downstream impacts. Legal battles have ensued, and in August 2026, the Court of Arbitration rejected India's unilateral abeyance, ruling that the treaty remains in force and ordering interim restrictions on the Ratle hydroelectric project.

The broader implications of an institutional collapse in transboundary water management could erode hydrological data sharing, flood warning cooperation, and regional investment. With both India and Pakistan possessing nuclear capabilities, unresolved water disputes heighten the risk of regional military escalation. Global heating above 1.5 degrees Celsius further exacerbates these hydrological instabilities, prompting calls for international environmental diplomacy to avert a major humanitarian and security crisis.

As the Neutral Expert’s final decision approaches in July 2027, the primary question is whether both governments will accept credible dispute-resolution processes. A breakdown in transboundary governance could destabilize the region, increasing diplomatic costs and setting a volatile precedent. Ultimately, neither nation can insulate itself from the cascading economic and climatic consequences of a destabilized Indus basin.

stories.title: SK Hynix Pledges $1 Billion to Strengthen AI Chip Supply Chain
stories.summary:
South Korea’s SK Hynix has announced a 1.4 trillion won investment, equivalent to about $1.05 billion, to support domestic suppliers of semiconductor materials, parts, and equipment over the next five years. The funding aims to bolster the local supply chain and enhance competitiveness in the rapidly growing artificial intelligence chip market. The comprehensive supplier support program will span research and development, testing, mass production, and sales to help smaller firms overcome financial and technological barriers.

A central component of the initiative is the creation of a jointly funded testing facility named Trinity Fab, scheduled to open in May 2027. Located within the company’s new semiconductor cluster in Yongin, 40 kilometers south of Seoul, the facility carries a total budget of 874.6 billion won. SK Hynix will contribute 443.2 billion won, the central government 373.6 billion won, and local governments 57.7 billion won. The Yongin complex is part of a broader plan where SK Hynix intends to invest 600 trillion won to construct four chip fabrication plants.

The Trinity Fab facility will feature a 3,305-square-meter cleanroom equipped with tools for lithography, etching, deposition, and inspection. Smaller subcontractors and suppliers will be able to evaluate materials and equipment using 12-inch wafers in conditions mimicking commercial lines, significantly reducing testing costs and time-to-market. An independent non-profit foundation will manage the facility to safeguard sensitive intellectual property and proprietary information.

In addition to the testing laboratory, SK Hynix will provide up to 50 percent of initial development costs in advance under its research support scheme, offering compensation even if projects fail to meet targets. Furthermore, SK Hynix and financial institutions are partnering with the Korea Trade Insurance Corporation to provide 2 trillion won in financing, alongside low-interest loans and technical consulting for smaller suppliers.

stories.title: Deadly Fire Sweeps Through Phuket Commercial Shophouse in Thailand
stories.summary:
A fierce fire erupted early Monday morning in a commercial shophouse on the southern resort island of Phuket, Thailand, resulting in the deaths of 11 people and leaving 16 others injured. Police reported that the destructive blaze originated inside a building that housed a vehicle rental business before rapidly spreading to several neighboring properties located in the town area near the popular Patong beach on Phuket’s western coast.

Thai authorities stated that the fire began at approximately 3:17 a.m., prompting an emergency response that took firefighters about two hours to bring the flames under control. Among the 16 injured victims, 15 were identified as Thai nationals, while one was a citizen of Myanmar. Law enforcement officials confirmed that no foreign tourists were among the casualties or the injured individuals.

The precise origin and cause of the deadly blaze remain under active investigation by local authorities. This incident occurred just four months after another major fire at a Bangkok bar claimed the lives of at least 27 people, drawing renewed attention to commercial fire safety standards across the country.

stories.title: World Bank Rates Implementation of $370m National Health Programme Satisfactory
stories.summary:
The World Bank has given a satisfactory rating to the execution progress of its $370 million National Health Support Programme operating across Punjab, Sindh, and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Effective since October 2022, the initiative strives to advance universal health coverage by bolstering primary-level healthcare services, ensuring equitable access, and improving quality. The World Bank contributed roughly $259 million in financing, while additional resources came through grants and co-financing from the Global Financing Facility, the Gates Foundation, the Global Fund, and Gavi.

In its official disclosure, the Washington-based multilateral lender assessed both the overall implementation and progress toward development objectives as satisfactory, while categorizing the overall risk as moderate. The World Bank noted that the programme continues to deliver concrete results across provinces, with approximately 76 percent of the total funding already disbursed. Provincial authorities have demonstrated robust ownership, helping keep the remaining Disbursement Linked Results on track ahead of the December 31, 2027 deadline.

Out of its specific $259 million financing allocation, the World Bank has disbursed $205 million, equal to 79.3 percent. A separate $36.8 million co-financing facility is fully disbursed, whereas two other components of $35 million and $29 million have each reached 50 percent disbursement. The initiative utilizes a Program-for-Results financing instrument, which ties funding directly to the achievement of agreed milestones, building on prior universal health coverage reforms and the National Immunisation Support Project.

Health facility readiness scores under the programme have reached 80 percent in Punjab, 77.5 percent in Sindh, and 75 percent in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. However, modern contraceptive usage among women of reproductive age remains low at 30 percent in Punjab, 20 percent in Sindh, and 15 percent in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The programme addresses essential healthcare coverage, governance, accountability, and financing, aiming to enhance the availability of staff, medical supplies, and patient referral systems.

stories.title: Yen Holds Steady Against Dollar and Euro Amid Surprise Japan GDP Contraction
stories.summary:
The Japanese yen hovered near two-month lows against the dollar and remained largely unchanged against the euro during early trading on Monday. Markets are currently evaluating how an unexpected economic contraction in Japan during the third quarter will influence future monetary policy decisions by the Bank of Japan. Against major currencies, the yen traded at 159.69 per dollar and 176.04 per euro, remaining near thresholds where Japanese and United States authorities reportedly intervened earlier in the year.

Japan's economy, which is the second-largest in Asia, contracted at an annualized rate of 0.1 percent during the July-September period. This performance fell short of market expectations, which had anticipated 0.3 percent growth. Analysts at Capital Economics suggest that this third-quarter stagnation is unlikely to deter the Bank of Japan from pursuing further policy tightening at its upcoming December meeting, warning that the central bank may need to act aggressively as inflation threatens to surge.

Meanwhile, the US dollar has maintained broad strength against most major peers, driven by hawkish commentary from Federal Reserve officials and a hot October inflation report. These economic indicators have revived market expectations that the US central bank will implement aggressive measures to manage cost-of-living pressures. The US dollar index climbed to 103.44, marking its highest level since April 2025, as Federal Reserve President Jeff Schmid emphasized that the central bank still has work to do regarding inflation.

Interest rate futures tracked by the CME Group indicate a 93.9 percent probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike during the Federal Reserve's upcoming policy meeting concluding on December 9. Concurrently, the yield on the 10-year US Treasury bond decreased by 0.8 basis points to 5.143 percent. In cryptocurrency markets, bitcoin rose by 0.2 percent to $65,186.44 after a weekend sell-off, while ether gained 0.7 percent to reach $1,830.94.

stories.title: Gold Prices Rise Slightly as Investors Anticipate Rate Cues from Fed Remarks
stories.summary:
Gold prices experienced a modest increase during early Asian trade on Monday, rebounding from a multi-year low recorded the previous week. Investors are closely monitoring upcoming remarks from Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh to gauge the future trajectory of US interest rates. Spot gold advanced 0.3 percent to $3,892.42 per ounce, while US gold futures for December delivery increased 0.2 percent to $3,895.60 per ounce.

Precious metal bullion suffered a 4.5 percent decline last week, heavily pressured by rising oil prices that escalated inflation concerns and strengthened expectations of prolonged high interest rates. October producer prices in the US posted their largest annual gain in four years, reinforcing views that the Federal Reserve may continue raising borrowing costs following an anticipated rate hike next month. Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid and Boston Fed President Susan Collins both indicated that inflation remains too high, pointing toward the necessity of further monetary tightening.

Market participants currently price in a 94 percent likelihood of a 25-basis-point interest rate increase in December, alongside a 6 percent probability of a larger 50-basis-point move. Although gold traditionally functions as an inflation hedge, elevated interest rates raise the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion, dampening its attractiveness. Traders are also awaiting the release of the October Federal Open Market Committee meeting minutes scheduled for Wednesday.

Geopolitical tensions added further context to market conditions, with Saudi-backed forces retreating from clashes against Iran-aligned Houthis in Yemen, and Iran launching drones at US bases in Bahrain. In physical bullion markets, India experienced firm gold demand driven by domestic festive buying, while consumption in China remained subdued. Among other precious metals, spot silver rose 0.2 percent to $48.80 per ounce, platinum gained 0.2 percent to $1,497.12, and palladium edged up 0.1 percent to $1,001.40.

stories.title: Indian Equities Set to Open Higher Driven by Record Foreign Inflows
stories.summary:
Indian stock markets are projected to open higher on Monday, extending a positive trend that has lasted for three consecutive weeks. Investor sentiment remains bolstered by record-setting foreign fund inflows and a recent decline in international crude oil prices. GIFT Nifty futures stood at 25,258 points during early morning trading, signaling a strong start for the benchmark Nifty 50 index following its Friday close at 25,144.3 points.

During the previous week, the Nifty 50 and BSE Sensex gained 0.5 percent and 0.7 percent respectively, marking a notable turnaround for Indian equities after trailing other emerging market peers for the majority of the past two years. Data from the National Securities Depository shows that foreign investors purchased a net $8.9 billion worth of Indian shares in November alone, marking a record single-month acquisition. This heavy buying has reduced total foreign outflows for the year to $22.5 billion and brought the Nifty 50's annual losses to below 4 percent.

The broader market momentum has also been supported by a drop in crude oil prices and a shift in investor focus away from artificial intelligence stock sell-offs. Brent crude futures decreased by 0.7 percent to $95 per barrel on Monday, influenced by expectations of an emerging supply surplus. This surplus outlook stems from Middle Eastern shipments through the Strait of Hormuz nearing pre-war operational levels alongside US measures to facilitate domestic fuel transport.

In contrast to the positive sentiment in India, broader Asian stock markets declined following the sudden departure of Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia. Upcoming corporate earnings from the chipmaker and an initial public offering by Anthropic are expected to test the durability of the artificial intelligence-driven bull market.

stories.title: India's Voter Roll Revisions Lead to Muslim Detentions and Deportations
stories.summary:
India's recent electoral roll revision has resulted in the deletion of 130 million names nationwide, sparking controversy as the omissions disproportionately affect Muslims. The removal process has become linked to a government initiative aimed at identifying and expelling suspected illegal immigrants, even though losing voting rights does not legally establish foreign nationality. In West Bengal, where state elections occurred earlier in the year, 9 million names were cut, with Muslims accounting for roughly 70 percent of the 2.7 million deletions in closely reviewed areas.

Among those affected is 38-year-old Sahida Fakir from Mumbai, who was detained by crime branch police and subsequently deported to Bangladesh in July. Court records showed Fakir was among 149 people deported during that operation. Her family has filed a petition in the Supreme Court, pointing out that her parents and grandparents were registered voters in West Bengal dating back to India's first national election in 1952. Despite holding family documents and having appeared on electoral rolls since at least 2008, authorities asserted she presented a Bangladeshi birth certificate during an inquiry, a claim she disputed after her phone containing document copies was seized.

Similar detentions have impacted other individuals, such as utensil hawker Nasiruddin Sheikh, who was detained by police in Chhattisgarh after his name vanished from voter lists despite pending appeals before special tribunals. Sheikh and other detainees spent over a month in confinement at a facility featuring medical examinations and biometric registration before being released. While police and state lawyers maintained that West Bengal lacks permanent detention camps, holding centers have drawn scrutiny.

Home Minister Amit Shah defended the measures during a November 5 rally in Haryana, stating the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party's resolve to detect infiltrators, remove them from voter lists, and expel them. The issue carries heavy historical weight in West Bengal due to migration following the 1957 partition and the 1971 Bangladesh independence war. Legal challenges continue to mount as families fight removals they argue are based on untested executive assertions rather than verified citizenship statuses.

stories.title: Indian Rupee Faces Pressure From US Yields and Oil Prices
stories.summary:
The Indian rupee is anticipated to open largely flat, caught between opposing market forces that include rising US Treasury yields and volatile oil prices, alongside supportive foreign portfolio inflows. Currency traders projected the rupee to open within the 94.22 to 94.28 range against the dollar, following a Friday close of 94.24.

Earlier momentum that drove the rupee to a high of 93.60 faded late last week. The reversal was primarily triggered by a surge in US Treasury yields that pushed the dollar index to a high not seen in a year and a half. Currency professionals note that while higher US yields present clear headwinds, substantial foreign capital inflows prevent an outright bearish outlook on the local currency.

Overseas investors have injected nearly $9 billion into Indian equities during the month, marking a dramatic shift from heavy outflows of approximately $3.5 billion recorded in both September and October. Meanwhile, ongoing uncertainty regarding a potential United States-Iran agreement has spurred a recovery in oil prices from recent lows, compounding external pressures on the rupee.

Oil prices continue to navigate competing factors, receiving partial relief from reports that US President Donald Trump might withhold further military actions against Iran. Conversely, escalation risks persist following Tehran's assertion that it struck a US base in Bahrain, keeping external economic pressures active for the Indian currency.

stories.title: Asian Markets Fall as Nvidia Leadership Changes and Anthropic IPO Loom
stories.summary:
Asian stock markets declined following a volatile week marked by the sudden departure of Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia. Investors are preparing for upcoming corporate earnings and the initial public offering of Anthropic, which together will test the resilience of the ongoing artificial intelligence-driven bull market. Japan's Nikkei fell 0.6 percent, South Korea dropped 0.2 percent, and MSCI's broader index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan eased 0.1 percent.

Nvidia has experienced a significant valuation drop, with its market cap falling from about $5.8 trillion in early October to $3.9 trillion by Friday, according to LSEG data. Analysts forecast 90 percent earnings growth on $109 billion in revenue for Nvidia's fiscal third quarter, though market participants remain focused on whether the chipmaker will maintain its bullish outlook under new leadership. Meanwhile, trading for Claude chatbot creator Anthropic is scheduled to commence just days after Nvidia's earnings, serving as another barometer for artificial intelligence sentiment.

In monetary policy developments, markets await the minutes from the US Federal Reserve's October policy meeting, alongside numerous speeches from Fed officials. While Fed funds futures indicate a quarter-point rate hike next month is largely expected, expectations for a larger 50-basis-point increase remain low. US Treasury yields remained steady following a significant weekly decline, with two-year yields at 4.8652 percent and ten-year yields holding above 5 percent at 5.1433 percent.

In commodities, oil prices remained mostly steady after enduring two weeks of declines, with Brent futures down 0.2 percent to $95.69 a barrel and US crude futures edging up to $88.68. Non-interest-bearing gold rebounded 0.3 percent to $3,891 an ounce after sliding 4.6 percent the previous week. Additionally, US President Donald Trump is scheduled to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the APEC forum in Shenzhen to discuss nuclear arms reduction and the conflict involving Iran.

stories.title: Houthis Release 600 Prisoners as Yemeni Forces Withdraw Near Strategic Strait
stories.summary:
Yemen's Houthis released 600 members of Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces on Sunday in what the International Committee of the Red Cross termed the largest unilateral prisoner release in recent months. The release coincided with a strategic military redeployment by pro-government forces, who withdrew from an area overlooking the vital Bab al-Mandeb Strait and left the Houthis in control of the maritime chokepoint.

The government retreat grants the Houthis enhanced leverage over global shipping lanes. Concurrently, fighting intensified as a Houthi missile attack killed eight people near Aden, while 12 others sustained injuries during an assault on a checkpoint in Lahj province. Military and government sources reported that Houthi fighters seized control of two districts in Lahj and advanced to within 60 kilometers of Aden, positioning themselves at the Al-Kharaz camp.

Amid these developments, the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Ansarallah forces announced it intercepted two ballistic missiles launched toward Riyadh, alongside two drones neutralized in the eastern region of Saudi Arabia. The kingdom has faced a surge in Houthi cross-border attacks targeting energy infrastructure, transport facilities, and the financial district in Riyadh since hostilities reignited in July, following the breakdown of a 2022 ceasefire.

The renewed conflict in Yemen has claimed more than 1,600 lives and displaced over 300,000 people since July, according to United Nations figures. The broader civil conflict originally erupted in 2014 when Houthi-led Ansarallah forces initiated an offensive against the government and captured large portions of the country, including the capital city.

stories.title: Global Oil Prices Decline Due to Forecasted Supply Surplus
stories.summary:
Crude oil prices dropped on Monday as markets anticipated a shift toward a global supply surplus. Brent futures decreased by 47 cents, or 0.49%, to settle at $95.37 a barrel by 0145 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude dropped 23 cents, or 0.26%, reaching $88.33. This downward movement followed a steep weekly loss of 16% for Brent and 13% for WTI. The market shift is driven by the nearly complete recovery of Middle East shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, bringing volumes close to pre-war levels despite ongoing shipping attacks.

The International Energy Agency forecasted that the world oil market will return to a surplus in the final quarter of the year, averaging 105 million barrels per day, which exceeds predicted demand by 1.7 million barrels daily. This marks a reversal from earlier deficit projections. Additionally, the agency noted that 71 million barrels from its emergency reserves will be released by the end of February, including 15 million barrels of diesel.

Downward pressure on prices was further reinforced by US President Donald Trump extending a 90-day waiver of the Jones Act. This decision allows foreign-flagged vessels to more easily transport oil, gasoline, and diesel between domestic ports, expanding the availability of active tankers. Despite loosening supply fundamentals, KCM Trade chief analyst Tim Waterer pointed out that elevated shipping rates continue to place a floor on oil prices. These high rates persist due to risks faced by tankers navigating the Strait of Hormuz and vessel bottlenecks inside the waterway.

The market environment remains tense as geopolitical risks continue alongside logistical hurdles. Highlighting ongoing dangers in the region, state media reported that an oil tanker caught fire on Sunday night after striking a naval mine located east of the Strait of Hormuz, according to the Iranian navy.

stories.title: Punjab Chief Minister Announces Province's First AI-Powered Climate Observatory
stories.summary:
Construction is actively underway in Lahore for the Punjab Climate Observatory, hailed by provincial Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif as a milestone in regional climate management. Announced on Sunday, the facility is described as the first project of its kind in Pakistan. It will utilize an artificial intelligence-driven climate intelligence system to perform real-time monitoring of air quality, water resources, soil health, and weather conditions across the province.

The initiative gained formal approval in May 2025 following a comprehensive feasibility review encompassing budgetary needs, equipment acquisition, and land procurement. Technical evaluations were previously submitted by the University of Engineering and Technology in Lahore, and the chief minister directed authorities to accelerate construction progress back in June.

According to CM Maryam, the observatory will significantly enhance early warning systems, weather forecasting, and flood predictions, thereby boosting disaster preparedness. The center will also feature research laboratories and environmental data resources designed to offer learning opportunities for young climate scientists and foster international scientific cooperation.

Ultimately, the project aims to support evidence-based policymaking, public awareness, and sustainable resource management. Officials hope the facility will bolster agricultural resilience, forest protection, water conservation, and disaster resilience, positioning Punjab as a regional leader in climate innovation and environmental protection.

stories.title: UN Agency Warns Punjab Faces Severe Water Shortages Across All Sectors
stories.summary:
A comprehensive assessment published by the Food and Agriculture Organisation warns that water demand in Punjab currently outstrips available supply across all sectors. The United Nations specialized agency reported that the province's groundwater is depleting at a rate of roughly 5.5 billion cubic metres annually over a five-year period, while surface water resources face mounting stress. Findings were derived from annual water accounts spanning five water years from 2012 to 2017, utilizing expert advice from specialists including former Wapda chairman Shamsul Mulk and former Irsa chairman Rao Irshad Ali Khan.

The report emphasizes the urgent need for integrated water resource management and recommends creating a special commission to conduct a single review of provincial water policies, institutional mandates, and strategies. This proposed commission would ensure policy coherence, establish assessment mechanisms for transboundary projects, and set up a provincial coordination cell within the Planning and Development Department. Urban areas are experiencing acute supply gaps due to shrinking freshwater access and groundwater depletion, while agricultural production faces increasing risks.

To bridge the supply-demand gap and sustain the groundwater aquifer, the analysis estimates that Punjab requires an additional 10 billion cubic metres of usable water yearly. Freshwater shortages have forced greater reliance on low-quality recycled water and heightened pollution from agro-chemicals and urban wastewater. Furthermore, river flows through the province have dropped by about 30 billion cubic metres following the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty with India, leaving natural landscapes diminished and wetlands accounting for only 1.7 per cent of the area.

The technical diagnosis identified several critical challenges, including growing spatio-temporal water scarcity, continuous groundwater exhaustion, inter-sectoral competition, and deficiencies in data collection. The report advises expanding land-use classification systems province-wide and implementing timely interventions to boost surface water resources, improve groundwater recharge, and develop inter-seasonal water transfer mechanisms.

stories.title: Punjab Sugar Mills Defy Government Mandate to Begin Crushing Season
stories.summary:
Most sugar mills across Punjab failed to initiate sugarcane crushing operations on Sunday, directly defying a provincial government mandate requiring activity to commence by November 15. An official from the Pakistan Sugar Mills Association confirmed that Ramzan Sugar Mills was the sole facility to comply with the directive, which was issued by the Punjab Food Safety and Consumer Protection Department on behalf of the governor. The official notification ordered millers to purchase crops and start crushing within 24 hours while instructing deputy commissioners to enforce compliance.

Both the PSMA north zone and various farmer groups scheduled press conferences to address the unfolding standoff. Khalid Hussain Bath, a farmers' group president, criticized the government notification as ineffective, noting that mills remained idle in Punjab and operations had not started in Sindh. Bath stated that the delays inflict financial losses on growers who are already burdened by market uncertainties and inflated prices for di-ammonium phosphate fertiliser. He urged Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to intervene and demanded an immediate announcement of a sugarcane support price alongside requirements for mills to purchase all approved crop varieties.

Official sources indicated that sugarcane prices are intended to be determined through a market-based mechanism while the provincial government monitors rates to protect growers. Cultivation data shows sugarcane covers 2.452 million acres in Punjab this year, representing a 16 percent increase compared to the previous year. Earlier in the month, Minister for National Food Security and Research Rana Tanveer Hussain announced that the Sugar Advisory Board had fixed November 15 for the nationwide opening of the crushing season following consultations with provincial governments, the PSMA, and cane commissioners.

During the advisory board meeting, attended by a PSMA delegation led by Chaudhry Zaka Ashraf, Minister Hussain warned of strict penalties for any mill failing to launch operations on time. He emphasized that the payment of dues to farmers must be guaranteed before crushing begins, asserting that all official decisions are designed to safeguard growers from exploitation.

stories.title: آزاد کشمیر کے مختلف علاقوں میں بارش اور برف باری سے سردی میں اضافہ
stories.summary: آزاد کشمیر کی وادی لیپہ اور وادی نیلم میں بارش اور برف باری ہوئی ہے، جبکہ استور میں بھی وقفے وقفے سے بارش اور برف باری کا سلسلہ جاری ہے۔ ان موسمی تبدیلیوں کے باعث وہاں شدید سردی پڑ رہی ہے اور جلانے کی لکڑی کی مانگ میں نمایاں اضافہ ہو چکا ہے۔ دوسری طرف ملک کے دیگر حصوں میں بھی مختلف اہم واقعات پیش آئے ہیں۔ پنجاب میں فضائی آلودگی بدستور برقرار ہے جہاں لاہور دنیا کے بڑے آلودہ شہروں میں دوسرے اور کراچی چھٹے نمبر پر موجود ہے۔ مالی سال 2026-27 کے پہلے چار ماہ کے دوران ملکی برآمدات 11 ارب 37 کروڑ ڈالر کی بلند ترین سطح پر پہنچ گئی ہیں، اور تاریخ میں پہلی بار صوبوں نے وفاق کو 57 ارب 46 کروڑ روپے کی گرانٹ فراہم کی ہے۔ اس کے علاوہ، مالاکنڈ، دیر بالا، سوات، باجوڑ اور گردونواح میں زلزلے کے جھٹکے محسوس کیے گئے ہیں، اور اسلام آباد میں اقتصادی تعاون تنظیم کے تیسویں وزرائے خارجہ اجلاس کا ایجنڈا طے کر لیا گیا ہے۔ دریں اثنا، لاہور میں مرغی کے گوشت، سبزیوں اور ایل پی جی کی بڑھتی ہوئی قیمتیں تاحال قابو سے باہر ہیں جبکہ پولیس ایک تیرہ سالہ گھریلو ملازمہ کے جسم پر تشدد کے نشانات پائے جانے کے واقعے کی مزید تفتیش کر رہی ہے۔

stories.title: CDA revises Islamabad cricket stadium cost to Rs16.7bn
stories.summary:
The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has finalised a modified PC-I for the upcoming Islamabad Cricket Stadium, raising the total estimated cost of the project from Rs11.9 billion to Rs16.7 billion. According to a CDA official, the adjustment accounts for expanded components including the grey structure, finishing, lighting, heating, ventilation and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems, ground and pitch preparation, and a security camera system. The venue's planned seating capacity was also increased to 35,000, which will make it Pakistan's largest cricket stadium.

The project is slated to be built at the foothills of the Margalla Hills near Sector D-12, a site within Zone III where construction is generally restricted, though sports and recreational activities are permitted. The CDA previously received a bid of Rs8.9 billion from a joint venture of Habib-ZKB-EA, which included Rs5.8 billion for the three-tier stadium structure and Rs3.1 billion for external works such as three kilometres of three-lane roads. After securing a Rs400 million rebate, the contract amount was reduced to Rs8.5 billion.

Regarding the construction timeline, a CDA official stated that the bidding process for Phase-I, covering the grey structure and road network, is complete, with groundbreaking scheduled shortly and completion expected within six months. The authority intends to launch the tendering process for Phase-II following official approval of the PC-I, aiming to finalise the entire project within one year. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi recently announced that groundbreaking would occur within 10 days.

A Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) official noted that if the venue is finished on time, Pakistan hopes to host matches for the ICC Women’s T20 World Cup in 2028. Previous attempts by the PCB to construct a stadium at Shakarparian were abandoned following Supreme Court directives, leading the CDA to undertake the current construction directly.

stories.title: صدر اور وزیراعظم کے عالمی یوم برداشت پر اہم پیغامات جاری
stories.summary:
عالمی یومِ برداشت کے موقع پر صدر مملکت آصف علی زرداری اور وزیراعظم شہباز شریف نے اپنے الگ الگ پیغامات جاری کیے ہیں۔ صدر مملکت نے اپنے بیان میں اس بات پر زور دیا کہ اسلام انسان کو ہمدردی، انصاف اور انسانی وقار کے احترام کا درس دیتا ہے، اور قانون کی نظر میں تمام شہری مکمل طور پر برابر ہیں اور مساوی تحفظ کے حق دار ہیں۔ انہوں نے خبردار کیا کہ نوجوانوں کو آن لائن سرگرمیوں میں بھی اس احترام کو ملحوظ رکھنا چاہیے کیونکہ غیر محتاط الزام تراشی یا نفرت انگیز پیغامات انسانی زندگیوں کے لیے خطرناک ثابت ہو سکتے ہیں، لہذا عوامی اداروں کو امتیازی سلوک اور تشدد پر اکسانے والوں کے خلاف سختی سے نمٹنا چاہیے۔

دوسری جانب وزیراعظم شہباز شریف کا کہنا تھا کہ تمام تر اختلافات کے باوجود دوسرے افراد کے عقائد اور نظریات کا احترام کرنا ہی اصل برداشت کا مفہوم ہے۔ انہوں نے اس عزم کا اظہار کیا کہ اسلامی تعلیمات ہمیں صبر، برداشت، ہمدردی، عدل و انصاف اور احترامِ انسانیت کا راستہ دکھاتی ہیں جو کہ ہمارے لیے مشعلِ راہ ہیں۔ وزیراعظم نے علمائے کرام، اساتذہ، میڈیا اور خاص طور پر نوجوان نسل سے اپیل کی کہ وہ معاشرے سے تعصب کے رجحان کو مکمل طور پر مسترد کریں۔

اس دن کی مناسبت سے جاری ہونے والے ان پیغامات کا بنیادی مقصد معاشرتی ہم آہنگی کو فروغ دینا اور رواداری کی فضا قائم کرنا ہے۔ ایسے بیانات موجودہ ملکی حالات میں مختلف طبقات کے درمیان فاصلے مٹانے اور باہمی احترام کے فروغ کے لیے انتہائی اہمیت کے حامل ہیں۔ حکومت اور ریاستی سطح پر اس طرح کے پیغامات کے ذریعے شہریوں کو ذمہ دارانہ رویہ اپنانے اور قانون کے دائرے میں رہتے ہوئے زندگی گزارنے کی تلقین کی جاتی ہے۔

stories.title: Pakistan proposes virtual green university and youth fund at COP31
stories.summary:
Pakistan has introduced proposals to establish a virtual green university through international academic partnerships and a dedicated fund aimed at supporting youth-led climate innovation.
